note: Claim ledger. Each claim names a profile, one evidence tier, an artifact that exists, the profile fields it depends on and a standing. A claim that depends on a field tagged tier4-community, tier5-emulator-hint, inference or unknown-default-chosen is provisional. Vocabulary: docs/evidence-tiers.md.

claims.statement: On the CP-1600 manual's reading, a push writes the word at the address held in R6 and then increments R6, and a pull first decrements R6 and then reads, so the stack grows toward higher addresses.
claims.note: The expectation comes from three manual pages read in plan 01-02 (C17 resolved-primary). Applying the CP-1600 manual to the CP-1610 is an inference logged as C31 in the discrepancy log, so the claim stays provisional.

claims.statement: The NTSC STIC part of this profile is the AY-3-8900-1, operated from a 3.579545 MHz crystal.
claims.note: All three fields carry tier1-primary-doc tags citing the 1980 data catalog; the page was a research-era reading and is re-read when the profile is next revised. The claim states only the printed figure; the exact crystal ratio is logged as C9. The STIC1A variant is not modelled.

claims.statement: A nominal NTSC frame is 262 scanlines times 57 CPU cycles, which is 14,934 CPU cycles and 59,736 master ticks.
claims.note: The scanline and per-scanline counts are tier4-community and the ticks per CPU cycle are an inference, so the weakest-field rule makes the claim provisional. A primary source or a measurement would resolve it.

claims.statement: The CP-1600 manual marks shifts and the instructions EIS, DIS, TCI, CLRC and SETC as not interruptible and says nothing about HLT, SDBD and MVO.
claims.note: This records what the manual pages say (C19 partial). Whether the silent cases are interruptible on the CP1610 is unresolved, and applying the CP-1600 manual to the CP1610 is an inference logged as C31.

claims.statement: Every one of the 1024 10-bit opcode decle patterns maps to exactly one most-specific row of the CP-1610 family table, with one documented coincidence (0010 111 111: TSTR R7, JR R7 and MOVR R7,R7).
claims.note: The table is transcribed from the CP-1600 manual page images and the coverage check proves the rows tile the decle space, not that any encoding, cycle count or status bit was read correctly. Applying the CP-1600 manual to the CP1610 is an inference logged as C31, so the claim stays provisional.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, the read and write widths of every address, the mirror extents of RAM and ROM rows and the behaviour-changing row boundaries, observed through the real bus functions, together with the device, impl and gate labels (and stub mirror labels) reported by the introspection function, equal the structural columns of the sourced literal map.
claims.note: Evidence: case memmap.dump.matches-literal of suite memmap writes the decode dump of all 65,536 addresses in both views, and the memmap gate step compares the dev and release dumps with the literal (plan 03-06). A pass shows transcription consistency between the literal map and the runtime decode, not hardware truth. Widths, RAM and ROM mirrors and the boundaries where they change are behavioural; the device, impl and gate columns and the mirror of stub and undriven rows are declarative labels from ivs_memsys_describe. Several depended-on fields are tier4-community, inference or unknown-default-chosen (C5, C11, C20, C21, C60, C61, C62, C64, C70, C75), so the claim is provisional; a D10 decode probe on owner hardware would raise it. Plan 05-04: the PSG region became a real device (psg8, upper byte 0, C64); its register rows are split by width and carry C70 and C75, and the shape register and the two port registers are declared exception rows whose store is observed in the register storage. Plan 06-06: the five STIC regions became the real device stic14 (A-01); their rows are split by the register widths of the independent register literal, the write-only stored registers are x=reads-zero rows, the two strobe registers are a new declared exception x=strobe (nothing is stored, the access has a machine-level effect), the collision registers read $FC00 OR their stored bits, and the read alias of $0040 mirrors the register file.

claims.statement: The core's IVSC v1 layer-1 parser accepts every positive record and refuses every malformed record of fixture FX-ivsc-vectors with the status, reason, segment index and byte offset that docs/formats/ivsc-v1.md documents for it, and the seeded fuzz family of suite ivsc reaches every refusal reason of that specification without breaking the parser's refusal, determinism and round-trip invariants.
claims.note: Evidence: suite ivsc in the dev (ASan and UBSan) and release presets, with the parse-level records of data/cart/ivsc-parse.json and the fuzz family ivsc.fuzz.* (eight fixed seeds and ivsc.fuzz.reasons-covered, plan 03-08); six named faults in data/expected/faults/ivsc.ids show that the fixtures catch the loss of a parser rule. The expectations come from the project's own specification, and every positive trailer and whole-file digest was computed with cmake -E sha256sum, independently of the core's SHA-256. IVSC is the project's own format, so this is conformance to the project specification, not to any hardware or third-party format. Layer 1 knows no profile; the claim names the profile whose cartridge fields admit IVSC v1. cartridge.slots is unknown-default-chosen (a scope choice), so the weakest-field rule makes the claim provisional. The layer-2 load into an instance is not covered here (plan 03-11).

claims.statement: From a power-on reset of profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1 through the public API, the project boot stub (contract 1) and the project-authored diagnostic ivs-diag-cpu-1 reach the hand-derived guest state of data/golden/diag-cpu-1.expect: the CPU halted, R0-R6 and the ten memory words 0200-0208 and 020F equal to the derived values.
claims.note: Evidence: run.diag.predicate in the dev (ASan and UBSan) and release presets reads the expected values from the assert lines of data/golden/diag-cpu-1.expect, whose derivation (16-bit arithmetic, the status-bit rules of pdf 45, the GSWD layout of pdf 56, the stack direction C17 and the printed instruction and cycle tables) was committed before the program first ran on the emulator; run.diag.slice and run.diag.repeat show that the result does not depend on how the run is sliced or on the instance. Shared-misreading risk: the same author wrote the listing, the derivation and the core, so all three can share one misreading of the manual; agreement among them is not independent evidence about hardware. Excluded: R7 and the flags at the stop (HLT and interruptibility policies C40, C45, C56), machine time (regression information only), and the stack word [0340]. The cartridge entry $5000 and the stack start $0340 are project conventions (C68). reset.r7 is tier4-community and cartridge.slots is unknown-default-chosen, so the weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional. This is a statement about the project boot stub and the project's own diagnostic only: not a statement about commercial content or any EXEC.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, the low byte that a guest reads at the controller port address after each one of the 31 controls is pressed alone, on port 0 ($01FE) and on port 1 ($01FF), through the real bus read and through the side-effect-free peek, equals the byte of the project literal data/input/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.literal.txt, and an idle port reads 0xFF.
claims.note: Evidence: suite input in the dev (ASan and UBSan) and release presets: input.single.p0.<name> and input.single.p1.<name> (31 + 31 cases, read from the literal, never from the generated table), input.idle.*, input.table.matches-literal, input.struct.* and the three wiki anchors input.anchor.wiki-idle, wiki-key1 (key 1 reads 0x7E) and wiki-key1-9 (0x5A); the gate step input compares the literal with the profile fields row for row and its controls show that a wrong byte, a duplicated or missing name, a missing tag, an unknown source and a profile mask mismatch are rejected. Oracle: the literal was transcribed in plan 05-01 (pin table and pin-to-bit map of the ConsoleMods page and the key-table image of the community wiki, both cached only, rights unknown) before any generator, profile field or implementation existed; each byte is pin-table arithmetic (0xFF XOR the grounded pins). Second read: a blind isolated reader derived all 31 rows from a copy holding only the control names and agreed on pins, cleared mask and byte on 31 of 31 rows (docs/input/second-read-record.md; tier source-expectation, second-read); it is the same model family reading the same two community pages, so it is a transcription cross-check, not independent evidence. Shared-misreading risk: the same author wrote the literal, the generator, the profile rows and the core, and the two sources are likely one lineage (C16); the claim says the core reproduces the literal, not that a console reads these bytes. Excluded: policy rows (a pair of controls, see CL-0010), the upper byte of a port read (C64), a port with no controller attached (C64), a port set to output (C65), the mapping of ports to physical connectors (C66). The control rows and input.line_idle are tier4-community and input.line_model is an inference, so the weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional; a D10 reader diagnostic on owner hardware (31 controls on each port) would raise it.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, when more than one control is closed at once the port byte is 0xFF with the union of the pins of every closed control cleared, and the 24 combination rows of the suite, the wiki anchor of keys 1 and 9 (0x5A) and the decodability counts of all 465 unordered control pairs equal the figures derived from the project literal; the rows of data/expected/input-policies.ids classed as policy are results of the union rule and not statements about what a controller reads.
claims.note: Evidence: input.combo.* (24 rows), input.pairs.union, commutative, monotone-clear and decodable-claims (all 465 pairs: key and side 36 of 36 and side and side 3 of 3 ambiguous, key and disc 180 of 192 ambiguous), input.anchor.wiki-key1-9, input.port.independence and input.combo.ports-independent, in the dev and release presets; the judge self-controls input.judge.table-row-changed and input.judge.direction-sense-flipped show that a changed literal row or a flipped direction sense fails the suite; the faults CTRL_UNION_AS_AND, CTRL_PORTS_SWAPPED and CTRL_NO_INVERSION are caught. Oracle: the union rule (ground-union line model, tag inference) applied by hand to the literal masks, plus the two wiki statements (key 1 reads 0x7E; keys 1 and 9 together read 0x5A; disc with side button uniquely decodable; key with disc or side, and two side buttons, not uniquely decodable). Second read: the 31 literal rows agree (CL-0009); the combination figures were derived by the author from the same rows, so they are one shared reading. Excluded and named: the policy classes disc-disc-adjacent, disc-disc-other, opposite-directions and three-or-more (C63, unknown-default-chosen: whether a disc can close two positions at once is unknown and no source says what the port reads), the classes key-disc, key-side and side-side as statements about hardware (they are inference results of the union rule), and every port-direction and unplugged case. input.line_model is an inference and the control rows are tier4-community, so the claim stays provisional; the D10 disc-closure probe on owner hardware would raise the policy rows.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, the same controller input schedule applied at CPU-unit start boundaries gives identical guest-visible state and identical input, memory and composite digests whatever the slicing of the run calls, and, for a poll instruction that starts at tick s, a controller change at tick s-1 or s is seen by that poll and a change at tick s+1 only by the next poll (contract C67).
claims.note: Evidence: input.boundary.start-minus-1, start and start-plus-1 (the poll start tick observed by single-stepping, so the test does not assume it), input.slice.guest-visible, input.iso.interleaved-instances, input.invariant.pulldown-derives-from-words and input.takeback.restores-pins in suite input; run.input.* and run.fuzz.* (seeded slicing fuzz) of suite run; the scenario variants of suite runner-process (one-tick-apart order variant, 1-tick and 7-tick slicing runs of diag-ctrl-psg-pass compared with the plain run); the faults INPUT_APPLY_AT_RUN_START, RUN_EVENT_AT_TARGET_ONLY, INPUT_LOG_SLICE_RELATIVE_TICK, INPUT_STATIC_CARRY, INPUT_PINS_NOT_RESTORED_ON_TAKEBACK and INPUT_PINS_NOT_RESET are each caught. Oracle: slicing invariance and equality of two runs of one schedule (an invariance, not an external reference), plus the boundary arithmetic written in the contract. This is a statement about the project contract C67 (an event takes effect at the first CPU-unit boundary whose start tick is at or after its tick, a one-instruction granularity), a policy with a profile-flag reversal path, not about the console, which may differ by up to one instruction; the granularity can change goldens that carry input. The artifact is the notes file that states the contract; the executable evidence is the tests named here. Excluded: what any real controller does within an instruction. input.controllers is a tier 2 field and input.line_model an inference, input.line_idle tier4-community, so the claim is provisional by the weakest-field rule. The determinism claim is repeatability on one implementation, not agreement with another.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, the register-number-level PSG model of the core (register file with the project address map, tone, mixer, noise, envelope and amplitude rules) reproduces every vector of data/psg/rules.json, each derived by hand from the cited pages of the AY-3-8910 data sheet, with the unprinted parameters taken from tier-tagged profile data.
claims.note: Evidence: suite psg in the dev and release presets (psg.reg.*, psg.tone.*, psg.mix.*, psg.noise.*, psg.env.* including the sixteen shapes, psg.amp.*, psg.ampenv.*, psg.dac.*, psg.reseng.*, psg.reset.*, psg.profile.* perturbation tests) and the gate step psg-vectors, which requires every rule to have a vector, every vector to cite a rule and a page, every unknown default to be a policy row and the pending lists to be empty. Oracle: the vectors were derived by hand from the 1980 and 1982 catalog pages of the AY-3-8910 before the engine existed (plan 05-01, the page reading is in docs/psg/reference-notes.md); rate vectors are closed-form bounds on the divide chains. Second read: blind readers derived the vectors of all 11 vector files without the expected values; of 120 vectors 90 agree, 7 were answered unknown, 21 are not comparable because the blinded copy omitted a fact (rule agrees where comparable) and 2 are convention differences (noise first bits, envelope restart phase) resolved by the recorded convention (docs/psg/second-read-record-*.md; tier source-expectation, second-read); the same model family read the same pages, so this is a cross-check of transcription, not evidence about any console. The model is the register-number-level behaviour of the data sheet part applied by inference to an AY-3-8914-class part (psg.part is tier4-community, C11; the step of 8 chip clocks and the clock ratio are inferences, C69 and C76; ticks_per_psg_clock is an inference). psg.mix.truth-table is polarity-invariant, so a flipped mixer sense is caught by psg.mix.and-tone0 and not by that row. Excluded: the register address map as a statement about the console (tier 4, C70), period 0, the noise register width and seed, the DAC levels, the envelope restart phase and read-back of the amplitude and shape registers (policy, C12, C71, C72, C75), the interrupt-entry bounds, and any claim about sound. Everything above is unknown-default-chosen, inference or tier4-community, so the claim is provisional.

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, a run emits a cycle-stamped PSG register-write log and integer chip-rate samples (one level per channel every 16 master ticks on an absolute grid from reset) that do not depend on how the run is sliced or on the size of the output buffers, that replay to the same chip state as the run itself, and whose write records equal the PSG writes in a CPU-side bus trace of the same run.
claims.note: Evidence: psg.sample.*, psg.slice.*, psg.chain.*, psg.buffers.*, psg.bounds.*, psg.log.* (framing, byte order, raw 16-bit value, strictly increasing ticks, no read records, no synthetic power-on records, window, replay-equals-run, log-versus-CPU-trace, effect boundary) and psg.fuzz.* of suite psg, run.* buffer cases, the runner (ivsr 2, audio chain re-hash, psglog asserts) and the installed-consumer replay compared by the gate step pkg-install, in the dev and release presets; the faults PSG_REG_WRITE_NOT_LOGGED, PSG_LOG_TICK_UNIT_START, PSG_LOG_TICK_SLICE_RELATIVE, PSG_SAMPLE_PHASE_RESET_PER_CALL, AUDIO_STATE_DEPENDS_ON_BUFFER, PSG_OUTBUF_PARTIAL_WRITE, AUDIO_SLACK_ZERO, PSG_LOG_RECORDS_PER_FRAME_CUT, RUNNER_AUDIO_CHAIN_CHECK_SKIPPED and RUNNER_PSGLOG_ASSERT_IGNORED are each caught. Oracle: invariance under slicing, replay of the log into a fresh chip, the log compared with a bus trace taken by the CPU-side wrapper, and the sample-count formula floor(now_exit / 16) - floor(now_entry / 16) computed independently. The statement concerns the register-number-level model and the project's own derived write list (the 11 writes of the diagnostic ivs-diag-ctrl-psg-1, CL-0014), not the AY-3-8914 or any console, and it is repeatability of the project's own contracts: the write instant within a CPU cycle and the sample alignment are decisions (C78, D-16), the raw 16-bit log value is a decision (C79), and the sample goldens are self-recorded. The reference PCM of plan 05-10 is outside this claim and outside the evidence path. Shared-misreading risk: the same author wrote the contract, the log, the trace wrapper and the replay, so a shared misreading of the contract is possible. Several depended-on fields are inference or unknown-default-chosen, so the claim is provisional.

claims.statement: From a power-on reset of profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1 through the public API, the project boot stub (contract 1) and the project-authored diagnostic ivs-diag-ctrl-psg-1, driven by the seven controller events of data/scenarios/diag-ctrl-psg-pass.ivss, reach the hand-derived guest state and PSG write list of data/golden/diag-ctrl-psg-pass.expect: the CPU halted, the end marker at 020F, the polled port 0 table 0210-0217 and port 1 table 0220-0227, the eleven programmed PSG registers read back, and a write log of exactly the eleven writes in the derived order with the derived addresses and values.
claims.note: Evidence: the scenario diag-ctrl-psg-pass of suite runner-process in the dev (ASan and UBSan) and release presets, and the ten run.diag.ctrl-psg.* cases of suite run, read the expected values from the assert lines of data/golden/diag-ctrl-psg-pass.expect, whose derivation (docs/input/diag-ctrl-psg-1-derivation.md, plan 05-01, commit 14a1904) was committed before the program existed; the contrast scenario diag-ctrl-psg-nokey (no input: the guest stays in its poll loop), the one-tick-apart order variant, the slicing variants and five program mutants (data/expected/diag-mutations-ctrl-psg.ids, one of them a negative control) show that the diagnostic can fail for the intended reasons and that its result does not depend on slicing. Shared-misreading risk: the same author wrote the controller and register literals, the derivation, the listing and the core, so all of them can share one misreading of a source; agreement among them is not independent evidence about the original console. The controller bytes rest on two community pages that are likely one lineage (C16) and the register map on one community page (C70). Excluded on purpose: machine time (the halt tick and the 81-cycle poll loop are regression information; branch counts are policy C29), the upper byte of a port read (C64: the guest masks every read, but the register read-backs of the file assume the default upper byte 0), the read-back of the envelope shape register (C75), R7 and the flags at the stop, and every register of the CPU. The weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional: reset.r7, input.line_idle, psg.regmap and the control rows are tier4-community, input.line_model is an inference, and cartridge.slots, psg.mixer.port_dir_bits and memmap.device.psg8 are unknown-default-chosen. This is a statement about the project boot stub and the project's own diagnostic only: not a statement about commercial content or any EXEC, and no audio quality or listening claim.

claims.statement: The installed package of profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, consumed by the separate consumer through the installed headers and archive only, replays the seven controller events of data/scenarios/diag-ctrl-psg-pass.ivss and reproduces the runner's input, audio and write-log digests of data/golden/diag-ctrl-psg-pass.digests, with the same observed domains, the peeked port 0 byte 0x007E after the first event, and the same guest tables.
claims.note: Evidence: the gate step pkg-install builds tests/installed-consumer against the moved install prefix with find_package(ivs) only, runs it on the build-tree images, requires its output to equal data/expected/pkg-consumer.golden and its ctrl.digest lines and observed-domain set to equal data/golden/diag-ctrl-psg-pass.digests (the cross-path agreement with the runner, one count rule); three in-step self-tests (ctrl-digest-drift, ctrl-domain-missing, ctrl-peek-wrong) show that a changed digest line, a missing domain and a wrong peeked value are rejected. The golden is self-recorded: the emulator produced these values, so the agreement shows that the installed package and the runner are the same machine, not that either is right. Excluded on purpose: machine time, the upper byte of a port read (C64), the shape register read-back (C75). The same weakest-field rule as CL-0014 keeps the claim provisional. This is a statement about the project boot stub, the project's own diagnostic and the packaging only: not a statement about commercial content or any EXEC.

claims.statement: The STIC register file of profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1, namely the 64 addresses of the project's register literal with their stored widths, the write-only read value, the collision read-back, the aliases at $4000, $8000 and $C000, the mode-select reads and the display-enable handshake, behaves as that literal states; the numeric access windows are policy figures and excluded.
claims.note: Oracle: the register literal (64 rows, plan 06-01 oracle commit eae8ca5, committed before any STIC code) read by the table test stic.table.matches-literal, the row tests stic.reg.*, stic.alias.*, stic.mode.*, stic.enable.seq.*, stic.blocked.* and stic.window.*, the memmap anchors memmap.anchor.stic-*, and the self-controls stic.judge.register-row-changed, stic.judge.window-edge-moved and stic.judge.blocked-write-applied. Shared-misreading risk: one author wrote the literal, the tests and the core, and the register map, the strobe and the alias reads rest on one community lineage (tier 4: the wiki STIC page, revision 15008, and the memory map page), so agreement among them is not independent evidence about the console. Blind second reads (plan 06-01 request, records dated 2026-11-12, tier word source-expectation, second-read): 64 of 64 register rows agree on role and class; the write and read masks are answered unknown by design (128 cells), so they are policy rows (C81, C86) and not second-read evidence. Excluded on purpose: the numeric windows (2,000 and 3,780 CPU cycles, C1, C2, C83, C94), the strobe sustain rule (C82), the power-on state (C85), collision behaviour (C87) and register decay (C88). The weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional: stic.regmap, stic.access_effects, stic.mode_select_addrs and the window fields are tier4-community and stic.power_on, stic.access_strobe_ticks, stic.access_gating_when_off and memmap.device.stic14 are unknown-default-chosen. No measured tier is used (D10).

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1 the VBLANK interrupt level and the bus-request windows occur at the times of the schedule printed in the timing note, with tile machine time exactly and the same instance bytes under any slicing of a run, and the number of bus windows that a frame can hold lies within the printed bound of 13 or 14.
claims.note: Oracle: closed forms and accounting identities written in the timing note before the code (a bus window starting at tick w resumes the CPU at w + 468, the event ticks 8,000, 15,120, 15,164 and 15,392 + 3,648 i inside a frame of 59,736 ticks, units tiling elapsed time), checked by stic.events.*, stic.irq.*, stic.busrq.*, stic.steal.*, stic.tile.units-equal-elapsed, stic.bounds.* (the bounds re-proof through the full machine with driven BUSRQ) and the slicing family stic.slice.one-call-vs-*, with the self-control stic.judge.late-grant-latched. Shared-misreading risk: the schedule is the author's reading of community figures (one lineage, tier 4) and inferences, so the tests prove that the model follows its own schedule and is repeatable, never that the console does. The tier is repeatability on purpose: no timing figure here comes from a tier 1 page. The policy numbers (windows, hold 114, interrupt width 3,791, release latency 2, power-on frame phase) are proven by perturbation of the profile fields and by accounting identities, never as expected values (C1, C3, C4, C7, C38, C52, C89 to C95). Excluded on purpose: the executed cycles per frame, which are an output of the model (C95), PAL and the STIC1A, and any statement about the instruction mix of commercial content. No blind second read covers timing (the four records are for registers, cards, frames and geometry). The weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional (tier4-community, inference and unknown-default-chosen fields). No measured tier is used (D10).

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1 the raw framebuffer has the published geometry of 159 by 96 positions with one byte per position, the published slot layout and the per-frame digest chain, and it is delivered at the frame event into a caller-owned buffer; palette, scaling and aspect are absent from the core.
claims.note: Oracle: the geometry literal (plan 06-01, commit eae8ca5) and the printed chain framing literal data/video/chain-framing.literal.txt, read by video.geom.*, video.layout.bytes, video.slot.*, video.chain.* (the chain recomputed from the delivered slots and from the printf recipe), video.buffers.*, video.boundary.*, video.stop.* and video.noop.null-buffer. Scope of the tier: the geometry counts (20 by 12 cards, 8 by 8 pixels, 7 pixels in the last column, 159 by 96 visible positions of a 167 by 105 grid, 16 colors) are source-expectation from the 1980 and 1982 catalog pages; the layout (header size, slot size, the capacity arithmetic) and the chain are repeatability, because no source states them. Shared-misreading risk: one author, one model family and the same pages for the count that sets 159 against 160 (C10, decision D8, one-field reversal video.last_card_column_px = 8). Blind second reads (plan 06-01 request, records dated 2026-11-12, tier word source-expectation, second-read): geometry: 20 keys read, 14 agree on value after spelling normalisation, 6 answered unknown (row-lines, header-bytes, slot-bytes, display-off-fill and two derived keys), 0 disagreements on a sourced value. Excluded on purpose: which 7 pixels are shown (C101), the border and window origin (C105), the content of a display-off frame (C99) and the row line count. The weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional (video.row_lines is an inference, video.last_card_column_drop, video.display_off_fill and stic.video_slack_frames are policy). No measured tier is used (D10).

claims.statement: For profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1 the Foreground/Background and Color Stack frames the core delivers equal the hand-derived frames of the project for the listed BACKTAB and graphics RAM contents, with the stated bit order, row order, last-column clip and Color Stack advance.
claims.note: Oracle: ten frame literals data/video/frames/F-A1..F-A5, F-B1..F-B3, F-D1 and F-D2 and the card table data/video/cards.literal.txt, derived by hand with a conservation check (plan 06-01, commit eae8ca5), compared by video.fgbg.*, video.cstack.*, video.card.*, video.probe.* (the 64-probe bit-role sweeps), video.meta.* and the machine-level video.fgbg.machine-* and video.cstack.machine-*; the self-controls video.judge.frame-row-changed, video.judge.card-bit-flipped, video.judge.cstack-persistent-pointer and video.judge.cs-roles-swapped, and the five card-rendering faults of the VID-04 registry lines show the comparison can fail. Shared-misreading risk: the card word layout, the bit order and the Color Stack rules rest on one community lineage (C96, C97, C103) and the same author wrote the literals and the renderer. Blind second reads (plan 06-01 request, records dated 2026-11-12, tier word source-expectation, second-read): frames: 10 read, 10 identical to the committed plane (the header carried the decoded fields, so this re-derives the plane, not the BACKTAB bit decode); cards: 64 bit-role rows read, 62 agree and 2 are a convention difference (the select bit 11 of the GROM and GRAM Color Stack words, recorded as a role against a fixed value, same semantics). Excluded on purpose: Colored Squares has no hand frame (C98), no GROM glyph data is used (the glyphs are project-authored bitmaps written by tests), no collision, no object plane (VID-05, Phase 8), no border (C105) and the display-off fill (C99). The weakest-field rule keeps the claim provisional (video.last_card_column_drop and video.display_off_fill are unknown-default-chosen; the Color Stack and card rules are community-sourced). No measured tier is used (D10).

claims.statement: From a power-on reset of profile intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1 through the project boot stub (contract 1), the project-authored diagnostic ivs-diag-stic-1 reaches the hand-derived guest state and the hand-derived frame of data/video/frames in Foreground/Background mode and in Color Stack mode, the mode being selected by one controller input at tick 0.
